paper.title: Curated test-time adaptation for multivariate time-series anomaly detection under distribution shift

official_code.command: python main.py DATA.NAME <dataset> TEST.TTA.SOLVER.BASE_LR <lr> TEST.TTA.STEPS <n> TEST.TTA.CANDI.GATING_INIT <g> TEST.THRESHOLD.ANOMALY_RATIO <alpha>

summary: CANDI freezes a pre-trained reconstruction-based MTS detector (MLP autoencoder) and, at test time, curates pseudo-false-positive samples via FPM (alpha-percentile validation threshold + Mahalanobis distance to a high-scoring validation reference set with a chi-squared 5th-percentile cutoff) and adapts a lightweight plug-and-play SANA residual module (per-variable TCN temporal embedding + inter-variable Transformer attention + per-variable linear projection, gated by tanh(g)) with SGD.

window_size.evidence: paper.md:1393 (Appendix: 'we set the window length to L = 10'); upstream/config.py:27

train_ratio.evidence: paper.md:1393 (last 20% of training data as validation); upstream/config.py:32; upstream/datasets/build.py:49-59

preprocess.value: z-score (sklearn StandardScaler fit on train split only)

architecture.value: Symmetric MLP autoencoder: Encoder Linear(win*D -> win*D/2 -> win*D/4 -> 128) with ReLU; Decoder Linear(128 -> win*D/4 -> win*D/2 -> win*D) with ReLU between layers; use_normalizer=False

sana_d_model.evidence: paper.md:1393 ('hidden dimension h = 512 for the SANA module'); upstream/config.py:135

sana_gating.value: nn.Parameter(GATING_INIT * ones(N_VAR)), applied as dec_out * tanh(gating)

epochs.evidence: paper.md:869 ('cosine learning rate scheduling ... for 30 epochs'); upstream/config.py:105 SOLVER.MAX_EPOCH=30

batch_size.evidence: paper.md:1393 ('batch size of 256 for both training and testing'); upstream/config.py:39

lr.note: PAPER DISCREPANCY: paper.md:869 states an initial learning rate of 0.001 for pre-training; the released source default is 1e-4 and no released script overrides the pre-training LR. Selected: source default 1e-4.

gradient_clip_norm.evidence: paper.md:1393 ('gradient clipping with a norm threshold of 0.5'); upstream/config.py:118

tta_optimizer.evidence: paper.md:1393 ('Adaptation was performed using SGD with Nesterov momentum of 0.9 and a weight decay of 0.0001'); upstream/config.py:91

Per-dataset per-alpha script values differ: SWaT 0.1 (alpha 0.5/1.0) and 0.03 (alpha 5.0); SMD_1-7 0.001 (all alphas); SMD_1-8 0.1/0.1/0.03; SMD_2-1 0.01/0.03/0.1; SMD_2-4 0.01/0.01/0.1; SMD_3-2 0.03 (all alphas).

candi_gating_init.evidence: upstream/scripts/SWaT/SWaT_alpha_5.0.sh:1 (GATING_INIT 0.5); paper.md:1393 searched {0.0,0.1,0.5}. SMD_3-2 uses 0.1 (alpha 0.5/1.0) and 0.0 (alpha 5.0); SMD_2-4 alpha 5.0 uses 0.0.

candi_min_samples.evidence: paper.md:1393 ('adaptation was performed only when at least 16 samples had been gathered'); upstream/config.py:86; upstream/tta/candi/adapter_candi.py:252,270

fpm_chi2_quantile.evidence: paper.md:260,280 (5th percentile of chi-squared with latent dimension d); upstream/tta/candi/adapter_candi.py:190,224 (chi2.ppf(0.05, df=latent_dim))

m2n2_gamma.evidence: upstream/config.py:81 (baseline only; not used by CANDI)

score_function.value: Reconstruction error: score = (1/(D*L)) * ||X - X_hat||^2 (mean over all non-batch dims of per-element MSE)
score_function.alignment: Higher score = more anomalous; anomaly if score > tau. tau = np.percentile(val_scores, 100 - ANOMALY_RATIO) (upstream/threshold.py:28-33; paper.md Eq.3, line 222).

anomaly_ratio.note: alpha is a reported evaluation protocol point, not a tuned hyperparameter; thresholds are derived only from validation anomaly scores, never from test labels.

discrepancies.resolution: Source default 1e-4 selected for pre-training; no released script overrides SOLVER.BASE_LR. Recorded so the reimplementation is reproducible and the difference is explicit.

discrepancies.source: per-dataset, per-alpha scripts fix different values
discrepancies.resolution: Per-run values are taken from the matching script; SWaT alpha=5.0 (lr 0.03, steps 5, gating 0.5) is the Default block. No new tuning is performed.

discrepancies.source: config.py:74 also offers 'best_f1' which uses test labels (upstream/threshold.py:34-38)
discrepancies.resolution: 'ratio' selected; 'best_f1' is rejected because it consumes test labels.

uncertainty: The reproduction target dataset is not fixed by the paper: SWaT (51 vars, downsample 5) and SMD sub-sets (38 vars, downsample 1) both appear. config.toml records SWaT because it is the source default (config.py:25) and the only fully resolved run artifact present (upstream/results/SWaT/MLP/5.0/config.txt).

TTA learning rate, adaptation steps and gating init are dataset- and alpha-specific in the released scripts; a single Default block cannot cover all of them. The exact pretraining LR used for the released checkpoints cannot be recovered from the repository (only the 1e-4 default exists).
Paper reports an average over three random seeds (paper.md:869); the released config only carries SEED=0, so a 3-seed sweep is a paper-level protocol detail left to the runner.
The repository contains an unexamined TSB-AD/ evaluation sub-directory; it is not part of the CANDI method entry point and was not used.
The paper's arXiv identifier (2604.01845) post-dates the retrieval environment; the repository commit 28c9679e503832f59e351208cde63657fcb51cad is the authoritative source.
Git clone of the official repository failed in this environment (HTTP 407 via proxy); all evidence above comes from the locally vendored upstream/ tree, which was verified against the paper.
